content.text: The foxml is pretty darned similar, so I think I can make it work relatively easily except for the disseminators.   I'm content to drop them with a warning message if that'll work for you
or throw an exception if they're encountered.
Mapping elements of our Univ. MD descriptive metadata schema to DC terms.
, for taking a look at this!  I have no problem with disseminators just being dropped.

I'm attaching a copy of a mapping document that we have created showing how we hope eventually to be able to translate some of our descriptive metadata from our homegrown XML schema to RDF properties.  I don't know to what extent this sort of mapping is a "pluggable" feature of the migration-utils as they stand right now, so if that's a totally separate issue please feel free to say so.  I thought it  doesn't hurt to pass along the file so you can see what we are hoping to achieve.
The lines in red just don't map well into a linked data context so our inclination is to just ignore those for now.
That is useful, though you're right it's another ticket.  I've created and linked that ticket.
I've created a PR that demonstrates added support for fedora 2 foxml.
I think I want to build out the new example distributable zip with more examples after I merge in changes associated with the last PR, so it's not ready to be merged.
If you want to play with it
, download that branch, go ahead.  There's a tailored  xml configuration in conf/fedora2-native.xml that ingests files from fedora2 directly from the object and datastream stores.
, to be clear, are you saying you do not want PR-28 reviewed with an eye towards merging it to master?

Nah, it's ready to go.... I wanted to let Joshua test it a few weeks ago before merging it.  When I merged in the last commit and marked it as "ready for test" that indicated that it was ready for review.
The code looks good, and the generated zip package is very helpful. Here is feedback from after running the build, unzipping the package and executing the following four ingests:
ingest successful, but: DS3 and DS4 do not exist
How are the blanknode, event resources being created? They do not reference the affected resource.
ingest successful, but: DS3 and DS4 do not exist
ingest successful, but: DS3 and DS4 do not exist
, I have been out since 07/01 and haven't had a chance to test this yet, but I will be back on Monday and am looking forward to giving it a whirl this week.

, I tested these 4 cases again and didn't experience missing datastreams.  Could you post the "id-minter.log" and the output of the command and then what you get when you request the appropriate resource so I can try to debug it?  As for the fedora2 example, you

get an error indicating that it won't transfer disseminators.  There's a very clear comment in the example configuration explaining how to override that.  I think it's critically important for the default example to bring to the users' attention that a) they have disseminators and b) they won't be migrated.  If the user points that configuration at that user's content and doesn't use disseminators, everything should migrate without issue.
Let me know if there's still an issue... I think these examples will make use of this tool eaiser for people, so would like to roll it in as soon as we are sure it works.

I tried to test, but I think it may be beyond me to set up the test. I managed to get maven to build, but I'm hitting null pointer exceptions that make me think I've failed to configure correctly, or to set up my exported Fedora 2 objects correctly.  I will probably need to enlist the help of one of the developers here to test this against our objects.

Mapping elements of our Univ. MD descriptive metadata schema to DC terms.

Thanks, Michael Durbin, for taking a look at this! I have no problem with disseminators just being dropped.

I'm attaching a copy of a mapping document that we have created showing how we hope eventually to be able to translate some of our descriptive metadata from our homegrown XML schema to RDF properties. I don't know to what extent this sort of mapping is a "pluggable" feature of the migration-utils as they stand right now, so if that's a totally separate issue please feel free to say so. I thought it doesn't hurt to pass along the file so you can see what we are hoping to achieve.

The lines in red just don't map well into a linked data context so our inclination is to just ignore those for now.
That is useful, though you're right it's another ticket. I've created and linked that ticket.

I've created a PR that demonstrates added support for fedora 2 foxml. https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/migration-utils/pull/28 I think I want to build out the new example distributable zip with more examples after I merge in changes associated with the last PR, so it's not ready to be merged.

If you want to play with it Joshua Allan Westgard, download that branch, go ahead. There's a tailored xml configuration in conf/fedora2-native.xml that ingests files from fedora2 directly from the object and datastream stores.
Michael Durbin, to be clear, are you saying you do not want PR-28 reviewed with an eye towards merging it to master?

Nah, it's ready to go.... I wanted to let Joshua test it a few weeks ago before merging it. When I merged in the last commit and marked it as "ready for test" that indicated that it was ready for review.

The code looks good, and the generated zip package is very helpful. Here is feedback from after running the build, unzipping the package and executing the following four ingests:
-------
java -jar migration-utils-4.2.1-SNAPSHOT-driver.jar conf/fedora3-exported.xml

  • ingest successful, but: DS3 and DS4 do not exist

-------

  • ingest successful, but: DS3 and DS4 do not exist

-------

  • ingest not successful
Sorry, Michael Durbin and Andrew Woods, I have been out since 07/01 and haven't had a chance to test this yet, but I will be back on Monday and am looking forward to giving it a whirl this week.

Andrew Woods, I tested these 4 cases again and didn't experience missing datastreams. Could you post the "id-minter.log" and the output of the command and then what you get when you request the appropriate resource so I can try to debug it? As for the fedora2 example, you should get an error indicating that it won't transfer disseminators. There's a very clear comment in the example configuration explaining how to override that. I think it's critically important for the default example to bring to the users' attention that a) they have disseminators and b) they won't be migrated. If the user points that configuration at that user's content and doesn't use disseminators, everything should migrate without issue.

Let me know if there's still an issue... I think these examples will make use of this tool eaiser for people, so would like to roll it in as soon as we are sure it works.

I tried to test, but I think it may be beyond me to set up the test. I managed to get maven to build, but I'm hitting null pointer exceptions that make me think I've failed to configure correctly, or to set up my exported Fedora 2 objects correctly. I will probably need to enlist the help of one of the developers here to test this against our objects.

Michael Durbin, I just re-ran the first test, after having unpacked the zip file into its own directory:
java -jar migration-utils-4.2.1-SNAPSHOT-driver.jar conf/fedora3-exported.xml

No errors, and on the surface everything looks great.
When I navigate in the HTML UI to the newly created resource that contains DS3 and DS4, and then into each of the datastreams, all looks good.
However, when I select "Download" on either of those datastreams — boom!
--------
HTTP ERROR 404
Problem accessing /rest/null73/e0/98/54/73e09854-8b9e-4732-9d41-e29d63704f25/DS2. Reason:
Not Found
--------
Notice the error message references DS2, and contains "/rest/null73/..." hmm? even though I am trying to download DS3 (as well as DS4, same message).

Also, I still have the question:
How are the blanknode, event resources being created? They do not reference the affected resource.

Once we get this first example sorted out, we can see if the other three are still an issue.

I fixed the bug for those datastreams.
